processSteps.stepName: Feedstock Purification & Anhydrous HF Electrolyte Preparation
processSteps.input: Anhydrous hydrofluoric acid (AHF 99.9%) and electronic grade ammonia (NH3 99.999%).
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Controlled reaction forming molten ammonium acid fluoride (NH4F·HF) electrolyte at 125°C; passes through molecular sieves to reduce moisture to < 10 ppm.
processSteps.output: Molten, dry NH4F·HF electrolyte ready for fluorination electrolysis.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We mix pure acid gas with ammonia to create a molten fluoride salt bath, baking out every drop of moisture so it won't ruin our electrochemical cells.

processSteps.stepName: Molten Salt Electrolytic Fluorination (NF3 Generation)
processSteps.input: Molten NH4F·HF electrolyte inside Monel electrolysis cell.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Direct current electrolysis at carbon anode (6-8 Volts, 2,500 Amperes): NH4F·HF → NF3 (Nitrogen Trifluoride, 75%) + N2O + N2 + HF + H2 (cathode byproduct); crude gas collected under positive pressure.
processSteps.output: Crude NF3 gas stream containing HF fumes, nitrous oxide, and nitrogen.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We pump heavy electricity through the molten chemical bath, splitting molecules apart to release nitrogen trifluoride gas bubbles from the anode.

processSteps.stepName: Caustic Scrubbing & Acid Fume Neutralization
processSteps.input: Crude NF3 gas stream.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Gases pass through counter-current potassium hydroxide (KOH 20%) spray scrubbers; HF is neutralized to KF salt, and N2O is decomposed over manganese dioxide catalysts.
processSteps.output: Acid-free, pre-purified NF3 gas with moisture < 50 ppm.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We wash the gas in alkaline chemical showers to strip away corrosive acid fumes, leaving clean neutral gas.

processSteps.stepName: Multi-Stage High-Pressure Cryogenic Fractional Distillation
processSteps.input: Pre-purified NF3 gas.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Compressed to 30 bar, cooled to -130°C in cryogenic cold box; Column 1 boils off volatile N2 and O2 overhead; Column 2 boils pure NF3 (bp -129°C), leaving trace fluorocarbons at the reboiler.
processSteps.output: Electronic Grade 5.0 NF3 gas (purity ≥ 99.999%).
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We freeze the gas down to -130°C inside giant insulated vacuum towers, distilling off nitrogen and oxygen to isolate 99.999% pure NF3.

processSteps.stepName: Cavity Ring-Down Spectroscopy (CRDS) & Gas Chromatography QA
processSteps.input: Distilled NF3 gas batch sample.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: CRDS laser spectrometer measures moisture (< 0.5 ppm) and trace CO2 (< 0.5 ppm); GC-MS certifies overall purity ≥ 99.999% and zero toxic perfluoroisobutylene.
processSteps.output: Certified quality analysis report meeting SEMI C-series gas standards.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Our laboratory shines specialized laser beams through the gas to verify that moisture is less than one speck per million.

processSteps.stepName: Cleanroom Automated Cylinder Filling & Helium Leak Testing
processSteps.input: Certified NF3 gas and pre-conditioned seamless steel cylinders.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Robotic filling under Class 100 cleanroom hood; cylinders pressurized to 150 bar, valves torqued to exact spec, and tested on helium mass spectrometer for leak rate < 1 x 10⁻⁸ mbar·L/s.
processSteps.output: Pressurized electronic gas cylinders ready for semiconductor fab delivery.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Cleanroom robots pump the gas at extreme pressure into seamless steel cylinders, seal the safety valves, and certify zero leaks before shipping.

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: A photomask (or reticle) is the master stencil of a microchip: it is a 6-inch square slab of synthetic quartz polished to atomic flatness, coated with an ultra-thin metal absorber film (chromium or molybdenum silicide), into which the chip's billion-transistor circuit design is carved using a high-energy electron beam. In the fab's lithography scanner, laser light shines through this mask, shrinking the master image four-fold and projecting it onto the silicon wafer. Every new chip design requires a custom set of 40 to 70 distinct photomasks (one for each layer of the chip), costing $1.5M to $4M per mask set. Monopolized globally by Photronics, Toppan Photomask, Dai Nippon Printing (DNP), and TSMC/Intel captive mask shops, India currently has zero commercial semiconductor mask fabrication capability. Building an Indian Photomask Center in Dholera SIR or Bengaluru gives Indian fabless startups and Tata Megafab fast turnaround mask tape-outs with 46% EBITDA margins.

twoProductionRoutes.name: Route A: 50 keV Variable Shaped Beam (VSB) Electron Beam Lithography
twoProductionRoutes.summary: Coating quartz mask blank with chemically amplified resist, loading into a 50 keV variable-shaped e-beam writer to raster-scan trillions of geometric circuit shots onto the mask, developing, and plasma etching the MoSi/Cr absorber film.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: High-purity 6025 quartz mask blanks pre-coated with Cr/MoSi and resist (from Hoya / Shin-Etsu).
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Universal gold standard for 100% of commercial 14nm, 28nm, and 40nm semiconductor logic and memory photomasks.

twoProductionRoutes.name: Route B: Multi-Beam Mask Writing (MBMW 260,000 Beams)
twoProductionRoutes.summary: Splitting a high-energy electron beam into 260,000 microscopic beamlets via a micro-aperture array, writing mask patterns in constant time regardless of design complexity.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: EUV multilayer reflective mask blanks and ultra-thin chemically amplified resists.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Next-generation writing for sub-7nm logic and EUV curvilinear masks where single e-beam writing times would exceed 30 hours per plate.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Semiconductor Photomasks & EUV/DUV Lithography Reticles transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: GDSII / OASIS Data Prep & Optical Proximity Correction (OPC)
steps.input: IC layout database files (GDSII / OASIS) from fabless chip design teams.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Supercomputing cluster runs inverse lithography (ILT) and optical proximity correction algorithms, fragmenting circuit curves into rectangular electron beam exposure shots.
steps.output: Fractured e-beam shot database verified for proximity effect correction.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We feed the chip designer's blueprint into supercomputers that add microscopic optical tweaks to compensate for how laser light will bend during wafer printing.

steps.stepName: Mask Blank Inspection, Loading & 50 keV E-Beam Pattern Writing
steps.input: Pre-coated 6025 quartz mask blank (Cr/MoSi + chemically amplified resist).
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: High-vacuum loading into NuFlare e-beam writer; 50 keV electron beam scans millions of shots per second, exposing resist to define nanometer circuit patterns over 8-16 hours.
steps.output: Exposed mask plate containing latent electronic circuit image.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Inside an ultra-high vacuum chamber, an ultra-precise electron gun shoots millions of atomic-scale dots of energy onto the quartz plate, drawing the master circuit pattern.

steps.stepName: Post-Exposure Bake (PEB) & Chemical Resist Development
steps.input: Exposed mask plate.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Bake at 110°C ± 0.2°C across 152mm quartz surface; develop in aqueous tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH 2.38%) to wash away exposed resist areas.
steps.output: Patterned organic resist mask over chromium/MoSi absorber layer.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We bake the plate gently to activate the light-sensitive chemical and wash it with developer liquid, leaving crisp stencil lines in the polymer.

steps.stepName: Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP) Dry Etch & Resist Strip
steps.input: Patterned mask plate.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Reactive ion etching in Cl2/O2 plasma (for chromium) or SF6/He (for MoSi); anisotropic chemical attack etches through metal absorber down to quartz; piranha acid wet strip removes remaining resist.
steps.output: Etched chrome/MoSi circuit pattern on ultra-flat quartz substrate.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Glowing gas plasma eats away the exposed metal, transferring the circuit pattern directly into the chrome metal film, after which all leftover plastic is stripped off.

steps.stepName: Deep-UV Die-to-Database Inspection & Nanometer Laser/E-Beam Defect Repair
steps.input: Etched mask plate.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: 193nm laser scans mask at 0.1 nm resolution, comparing image against original OASIS file; Carl Zeiss MeRiT repair tool shoots femtosecond laser or e-beam gas etching to fix any defect.
steps.output: 100% defect-free verified reticle plate.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: A laser microscope checks every square millimeter against the computer design. If any stray metal bump exists, a laser chisel evaporates it until it is 100% flawless.

steps.stepName: Protective Pellicle Membrane Mounting & Nitrogen SMIF Packaging
steps.input: Defect-free mask plate and fluoropolymer pellicle frame.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Automated cleanroom robot stretches a transparent dust-blocking pellicle film 5mm above the mask surface and hermetically seals it in a nitrogen-purged SMIF pod.
steps.output: Production-ready semiconductor reticle ready for fab scanner loading.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Robots mount a transparent protective dust cover over the plate and seal it into an airtight nitrogen travel box ready for the lithography scanner.

metadata.subtitle: Electron Beam Melting, Vacuum Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) & Diffusion Bonding of Copper, Tantalum, Titanium, and Tungsten Targets

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: Sputtering targets are the heavy metal cartridges that wire the modern microchip: inside high-vacuum plasma chambers, high-energy argon ions bombard a massive disc of ultra-pure metal (called a target), blasting off atomic metal atoms that fly through the vacuum and deposit as microscopic copper wires, titanium diffusion barriers, and tungsten contact plugs on the silicon wafer. A single 6N sputtering target requires extraordinary metallurgical perfection: 99.9999% purity (less than one contaminant atom per million), an ultra-fine grain size under 40 microns, and an airtight diffusion bond to a water-cooled copper backing plate. Monopolized globally by JX Nippon Mining & Metals, Honeywell Electronic Materials, Materion, and Plansee, these consumable metal discs sell for $8,000 to $45,000 each. Building an Indian Semiconductor Sputtering Target Plant in Hyderabad or Dholera (leveraging India's massive sovereign reserves of titanium from KMML and tantalum/copper refining) generates ₹740 Cr revenue with 45% EBITDA margins.

keyMetrics.marketOpportunity: ₹2,800 Cr ($340M) addressable Indian fab sputtering target market by 2030
keyMetrics.importDependency: 100% foreign import dependence (Japan, USA, Austria, Germany)
keyMetrics.sellingPricePerMT: High-Purity Copper Target: ₹6,50,000 ($7,800) | Titanium Target: ₹14,00,000 | Tantalum Target: ₹38,00,000 ($45,000) | Tungsten: ₹22,00,000

twoProductionRoutes.name: Route A: Electron Beam Melting (EBM) & Vacuum Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP)
twoProductionRoutes.summary: Refining metals to 6N purity under 10⁻⁵ mbar vacuum using multi-gun electron beam melting furnaces, followed by gas atomization into ultra-pure powders, vacuum hot isostatic pressing (HIP) at 1,200°C and 2,000 bar to achieve 99.9% density, precision CNC machining, and diffusion bonding to copper backing plates.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: High-purity electronic copper cathode, sponge titanium (from KMML), tantalum powder, and tungsten.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Universal benchmark for 100% of refractory metal targets (Tantalum, Tungsten, Titanium) and advanced alloy targets.

twoProductionRoutes.name: Route B: Vacuum Induction Melting (VIM) & Thermomechanical Cross-Rolling
twoProductionRoutes.summary: Melting copper and aluminum alloys in high-vacuum induction furnaces, casting ingots, multi-pass cross-directional cold rolling to break grain orientation, followed by recrystallization annealing.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: 6N electronic copper rods and ultra-pure aluminum.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: High-throughput, lower-cost manufacturing route for copper and Al-0.5%Cu interconnect metallization targets.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Ultra-High Purity 6N Metallization PVD Sputtering Targets transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: Electron Beam Vacuum Refining & Chemical De-Oxidation
steps.input: High-purity raw metal feedstocks (99.99% sponge titanium, copper rods, tantalum powder).
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Multi-gun electron beam melting under 10⁻⁵ mbar vacuum; high superheat volatilizes trace alkali metals and gas impurities (O, N, C reduced to < 10 ppm).
steps.output: 6N purity (99.9999% metal basis) ingots and refined master alloys.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Under super-high vacuum, an electron beam torch cooks the metal at thousands of degrees, boiling away trapped gases and microscopic dirt until it is 99.9999% pure.

steps.stepName: Vacuum Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) Powder Consolidation
steps.input: 6N atomized metal powders loaded into evacuated stainless steel canisters.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: HIP cycle at 1,200°C and 2,000 bar argon gas pressure for 6 hours; eliminates 100% of internal micro-voids, yielding 99.9% theoretical density.
steps.output: Dense, pore-free metallurgical billets with zero internal cavities.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We pack metal powder into steel cans and squeeze them inside a giant pressure cooker with argon gas at 2,000 times atmospheric pressure, fusing the powder into solid rock.

steps.stepName: Thermomechanical Cross-Rolling & Recrystallization Annealing
steps.input: Dense metal billets.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Multi-pass cross-directional rolling alternating 90° angles to break columnar dendritic grains; vacuum annealing at 850°C achieves fine equiaxed grain size (< 40µm) with random crystallographic texture.
steps.output: Uniformly textured target disc blanks with zero preferential grain orientation.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We roll the metal slabs back and forth in criss-cross directions, smashing the microscopic grain crystals into tiny uniform grains so the sputtering plasma eats the plate evenly.

steps.stepName: Sub-Micron CNC Turning, Milling & Cooling Channel Profiling
steps.input: Annealed target blanks and copper alloy backing plates (CuCrZr).
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: High-precision 5-axis CNC machining achieving dimensional tolerances ± 0.05 mm and surface finish Ra < 0.4 µm; cuts O-ring vacuum sealing grooves and water cooling channels.
steps.output: Precision-machined target tiles and backing plates ready for diffusion bonding.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Computerized diamond cutting tools carve the metal into circular discs and machine water cooling channels into the back so the target won't melt during use.

steps.stepName: High-Vacuum Diffusion Bonding & Ultrasonic C-Scan Inspection
steps.input: Machined target tile and backing plate.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Vacuum hot press diffusion bonding at 350°C under 15 MPa hydraulic pressure with thin interlayer foil; ultrasonic C-scan immersion testing verifies > 99.5% void-free bond area.
steps.output: Bonded target assembly verified for zero delamination risk.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We fuse the pure target tile to a heavy copper backing plate under vacuum heat and pressure, then scan it with ultrasound to prove there are zero unbonded spots.

steps.stepName: GD-MS Purity Certification, Cleanroom Degreasing & Nitrogen Foil Packaging
steps.input: Bonded target assemblies.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Glow discharge mass spec (GD-MS) certifies 6N metal purity; ultrasonic cleanroom degreasing in electronic IPA; double vacuum packaging in heat-sealed ESD barrier bags.
steps.output: Certified semiconductor PVD sputtering targets ready for fab delivery.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Our lab certifies 6N purity on a mass spectrometer, washes the target sparkling clean, and vacuum-seals it in double plastic bags for shipment to the chip factory.

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: If silicon dies are the brain of the computer, the ABF substrate is the nervous system: it is a multi-layer organic printed circuit board packed with microscopic copper wires and laser-drilled vertical vias that bridges the nanometer-scale electrical contacts on the silicon chip to the millimeter-scale pins on a motherboard. Every high-performance AI GPU (NVIDIA H100/Blackwell), server CPU (AMD EPYC, Intel Xeon), and automotive ADAS processor is mounted onto an ABF flip-chip BGA substrate. Without ABF substrates, advanced chips cannot be packaged. Global supply is fiercely concentrated across just 5 players: Unimicron, Ibiden, Nan Ya PCB, Shinko Electric, and AT&S (2 Billion market). Driven by Micron Sanand OSAT, Tata Electronics OSAT (Assam), and CG Semi Sanand, India requires millions of high-density package substrates annually. Building India's first FC-BGA substrate plant in Sanand GIDC (Gujarat) captures ₹3,200 Cr market demand with 44% EBITDA margins.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) High-Density FC-BGA Substrates transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: Core CCL Panel Preparation & Through-Hole Mechanical/Laser Drilling
steps.input: Low-CTE glass-epoxy core copper-clad laminate (0.4-0.8mm thickness).
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: CNC mechanical drilling of 100µm plated through-holes (PTH); alkaline permanganate desmearing cleans drilled glass fiber; panel electroplated with 15µm copper to form core circuit.
steps.output: Plated, patterned core panel forming structural substrate foundation.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We drill tiny vertical through-holes across rigid core boards and coat the walls with copper to build the central backbone of the substrate.

steps.stepName: Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) High-Vacuum Lamination & Hot Pressing
steps.input: Patterned core panel and Ajinomoto GX/GY dielectric film rolls.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Meiki vacuum laminator applies ABF film onto top and bottom faces at 120°C and 0.1 Torr; hydraulic hot press cures thermosetting resin, creating void-free 25µm insulating dielectric layers.
steps.output: Laminated panel with perfectly flat, void-free dielectric build-up layer.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: A giant vacuum machine heat-presses special Japanese insulating film onto both sides of the board without trapping a single air bubble.

steps.stepName: UV Laser Micro-Via Drilling (sub-25µm Blind Vias)
steps.input: ABF-laminated panel.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pulsed UV laser (355nm) drills 50,000 blind micro-vias per second through the dielectric, stopping precisely at the underlying copper pad with zero over-etching.
steps.output: Panel containing tens of thousands of microscopic vertical via holes connecting adjacent layers.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: A high-speed laser gun blasts 50,000 microscopic holes per second through the plastic film, stopping exactly when it touches the copper underneath.

steps.stepName: Permanganate Desmear & Electroless Copper Seed Layer Metallization
steps.input: Laser-drilled panel.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Potassium permanganate micro-etches laser drill resin smear; colloidal palladium catalyst seeds the dielectric surface; electroless chemical bath deposits a 0.3µm uniform copper conductive seed layer.
steps.output: Conductive seed layer covering all panel surfaces and blind-via sidewalls.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We dip the board into chemical cleaning baths and coat the entire surface with an ultra-thin chemical layer of copper so electricity can flow.

steps.stepName: Laser Direct Imaging (LDI) & Vertical Pattern Electroplating (SAP)
steps.input: Seeded panel and dry film photoresist.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: LDI laser exposes sub-8µm circuit patterns; vertical continuous plating (VCP) electroplates copper into channels, filling blind-vias solid and growing 8µm copper routing traces.
steps.output: High-density copper circuit layer with solid copper-filled micro-vias.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: A laser draws microscopic wiring patterns into photo-masking film, and electric plating baths grow solid copper wires into the open channels.

steps.stepName: Flash Differential Etching, Solder Mask, Surface Finish & 100% AOI/ET Inspection
steps.input: Electroplated panel.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Quick flash acid etch removes the 0.3µm seed layer without degrading 8µm traces; apply solder resist mask; deposit Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold (ENIG); 100% AOI optical and flying probe electrical testing.
steps.output: Certified high-density FC-BGA package substrates ready for OSAT flip-chip bonding.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We wash off the background seed metal, coat the board with green protective enamel and sparkling gold pads, and test every circuit with robotic electric needles.

processSteps.stepName: Core CCL Panel Preparation & Through-Hole Mechanical/Laser Drilling
processSteps.input: Low-CTE glass-epoxy core copper-clad laminate (0.4-0.8mm thickness).
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: CNC mechanical drilling of 100µm plated through-holes (PTH); alkaline permanganate desmearing cleans drilled glass fiber; panel electroplated with 15µm copper to form core circuit.
processSteps.output: Plated, patterned core panel forming structural substrate foundation.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We drill tiny vertical through-holes across rigid core boards and coat the walls with copper to build the central backbone of the substrate.

processSteps.stepName: Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) High-Vacuum Lamination & Hot Pressing
processSteps.input: Patterned core panel and Ajinomoto GX/GY dielectric film rolls.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Meiki vacuum laminator applies ABF film onto top and bottom faces at 120°C and 0.1 Torr; hydraulic hot press cures thermosetting resin, creating void-free 25µm insulating dielectric layers.
processSteps.output: Laminated panel with perfectly flat, void-free dielectric build-up layer.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: A giant vacuum machine heat-presses special Japanese insulating film onto both sides of the board without trapping a single air bubble.

processSteps.stepName: UV Laser Micro-Via Drilling (sub-25µm Blind Vias)
processSteps.input: ABF-laminated panel.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pulsed UV laser (355nm) drills 50,000 blind micro-vias per second through the dielectric, stopping precisely at the underlying copper pad with zero over-etching.
processSteps.output: Panel containing tens of thousands of microscopic vertical via holes connecting adjacent layers.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: A high-speed laser gun blasts 50,000 microscopic holes per second through the plastic film, stopping exactly when it touches the copper underneath.

processSteps.stepName: Permanganate Desmear & Electroless Copper Seed Layer Metallization
processSteps.input: Laser-drilled panel.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Potassium permanganate micro-etches laser drill resin smear; colloidal palladium catalyst seeds the dielectric surface; electroless chemical bath deposits a 0.3µm uniform copper conductive seed layer.
processSteps.output: Conductive seed layer covering all panel surfaces and blind-via sidewalls.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We dip the board into chemical cleaning baths and coat the entire surface with an ultra-thin chemical layer of copper so electricity can flow.

processSteps.stepName: Laser Direct Imaging (LDI) & Vertical Pattern Electroplating (SAP)
processSteps.input: Seeded panel and dry film photoresist.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: LDI laser exposes sub-8µm circuit patterns; vertical continuous plating (VCP) electroplates copper into channels, filling blind-vias solid and growing 8µm copper routing traces.
processSteps.output: High-density copper circuit layer with solid copper-filled micro-vias.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: A laser draws microscopic wiring patterns into photo-masking film, and electric plating baths grow solid copper wires into the open channels.

processSteps.stepName: Flash Differential Etching, Solder Mask, Surface Finish & 100% AOI/ET Inspection
processSteps.input: Electroplated panel.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Quick flash acid etch removes the 0.3µm seed layer without degrading 8µm traces; apply solder resist mask; deposit Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold (ENIG); 100% AOI optical and flying probe electrical testing.
processSteps.output: Certified high-density FC-BGA package substrates ready for OSAT flip-chip bonding.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We wash off the background seed metal, coat the board with green protective enamel and sparkling gold pads, and test every circuit with robotic electric needles.

productSpecification.substrateResinSystem: Bismaleimide Triazine (BT) / Epoxy blend (Tg > 210°C, ultra-low moisture absorption < 0.15%)

productSpecification.formFactor: Ultra-thin substrate thickness (0.10mm - 0.25mm) engineered for ultra-compact mobile memory cards and eMMC/UFS

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: While ABF substrates power giant AI processors, BT substrates power the mobile and memory world: they are ultra-thin, highly heat-resistant circuit boards made from Bismaleimide Triazine (BT) resin that form the packaging foundation for mobile DRAM (LPDDR5), 3D NAND flash storage (eMMC/UFS), smartphone application processors, and 5G RF power amplifiers. BT resin possesses extraordinary thermal rigidity: it does not warp or soften even at 260°C lead-free soldering temperatures, and absorbs virtually zero moisture. Commanded globally by Kinsus Interconnect, Simmtech, Daeduck Electronics, and Unimicron ($8.5 Billion market), BT substrates are the direct feeder material for Micron Sanand's DRAM/NAND packaging lines and Tata's mobile chip packaging. Building India's first BT Package Substrate facility in Sanand/Tamil Nadu secures sovereign memory packaging capacity with 43% EBITDA margins.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Bismaleimide Triazine (BT) Resin High-Frequency Package Substrates transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: BT Resin Varnish Formulation & E-Glass Fabric Impregnation (Prepreg)
steps.input: Bismaleimide Triazine monomer resin, curing catalyst, and electronic E-glass woven cloth.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pass E-glass fabric through BT resin varnish dip tank; vertical drying treater tower at 160°C semi-cures resin into non-tacky 'B-stage' prepreg sheet with 48% resin content.
steps.output: High-Tg BT prepreg rolls ready for lamination.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We soak ultra-fine woven glass fabric in liquid heat-resistant plastic and bake it into dry, flexible sheets called prepregs.

steps.stepName: Multi-Daylight Vacuum Hot Press Lamination & Copper Cladding
steps.input: BT prepreg sheets and 9µm electrolytic copper foil.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Stack prepregs between copper foils inside stainless steel press plates; evacuate to 0.5 mbar; apply 40 bar hydraulic pressure at 220°C for 150 minutes to fully cure thermoset resin into a rigid laminate.
steps.output: Ultra-thin, warp-free double-sided BT copper-clad laminate (CCL) panels.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We stack the sheets between paper-thin copper foil inside a high-temperature vacuum press, baking them solid under extreme pressure into flat copper boards.

steps.stepName: High-Speed CNC Mechanical Micro-Drilling (75µm Vias)
steps.input: Laminated BT panels.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Air-bearing spindles spinning at 300,000 RPM drive micro-tungsten-carbide drill bits, drilling 75µm diameter through-holes across the panel at 15 holes per second.
steps.output: Drilled panels with clean, burr-free through-holes.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Spindles spinning at 300,000 RPM drill thousands of hair-thin holes through the board to connect top and bottom circuits.

steps.stepName: Desmear, Electroless Copper Seed Plating & Pattern Etching
steps.input: Drilled BT panels.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Alkaline permanganate removes drill smear; palladium-catalyzed electroless copper deposits 0.5µm inside hole walls; dry film photoresist exposed via LDI; acid cupric chloride etches 12µm circuit lines.
steps.output: Etched fine-pitch memory circuit traces with conductive through-holes.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We wash the drilled holes with acid, coat the walls with copper, and use laser stencils to etch fine copper wiring across the surface.

steps.stepName: Solder Mask Application & ENEPIG Surface Finishing
steps.input: Etched circuit panels.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Curtain coat liquid photo-imageable solder resist; expose bond pad openings; deposit Electroless Nickel (3µm), Electroless Palladium (0.1µm), and Immersion Gold (0.03µm) (ENEPIG finish).
steps.output: Corrosion-resistant ENEPIG bond pads certified for ultra-fine gold and copper wire bonding.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We coat the board with green protective lacquer, leaving exposed copper pads plated with nickel, palladium, and pure gold ready for wire welding.

steps.stepName: High-Speed AOI, Netlist Electrical Testing & Strip Die Punching
steps.input: Finished panels.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: High-speed automated optical inspection checks bond pad dimensions; flying probe netlist tester checks 100% electrical continuity; precision die punch cuts panels into standard JEDEC memory strips.
steps.output: Certified BT memory package substrates ready for OSAT memory die attach.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Cameras and robotic electric needles test every single wire, and precision cutters punch the boards into finished memory strips ready for chip packaging.

processSteps.stepName: BT Resin Varnish Formulation & E-Glass Fabric Impregnation (Prepreg)
processSteps.input: Bismaleimide Triazine monomer resin, curing catalyst, and electronic E-glass woven cloth.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pass E-glass fabric through BT resin varnish dip tank; vertical drying treater tower at 160°C semi-cures resin into non-tacky 'B-stage' prepreg sheet with 48% resin content.
processSteps.output: High-Tg BT prepreg rolls ready for lamination.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We soak ultra-fine woven glass fabric in liquid heat-resistant plastic and bake it into dry, flexible sheets called prepregs.

processSteps.stepName: Multi-Daylight Vacuum Hot Press Lamination & Copper Cladding
processSteps.input: BT prepreg sheets and 9µm electrolytic copper foil.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Stack prepregs between copper foils inside stainless steel press plates; evacuate to 0.5 mbar; apply 40 bar hydraulic pressure at 220°C for 150 minutes to fully cure thermoset resin into a rigid laminate.
processSteps.output: Ultra-thin, warp-free double-sided BT copper-clad laminate (CCL) panels.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We stack the sheets between paper-thin copper foil inside a high-temperature vacuum press, baking them solid under extreme pressure into flat copper boards.

processSteps.stepName: High-Speed CNC Mechanical Micro-Drilling (75µm Vias)
processSteps.input: Laminated BT panels.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Air-bearing spindles spinning at 300,000 RPM drive micro-tungsten-carbide drill bits, drilling 75µm diameter through-holes across the panel at 15 holes per second.
processSteps.output: Drilled panels with clean, burr-free through-holes.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Spindles spinning at 300,000 RPM drill thousands of hair-thin holes through the board to connect top and bottom circuits.

processSteps.stepName: Desmear, Electroless Copper Seed Plating & Pattern Etching
processSteps.input: Drilled BT panels.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Alkaline permanganate removes drill smear; palladium-catalyzed electroless copper deposits 0.5µm inside hole walls; dry film photoresist exposed via LDI; acid cupric chloride etches 12µm circuit lines.
processSteps.output: Etched fine-pitch memory circuit traces with conductive through-holes.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We wash the drilled holes with acid, coat the walls with copper, and use laser stencils to etch fine copper wiring across the surface.

processSteps.stepName: Solder Mask Application & ENEPIG Surface Finishing
processSteps.input: Etched circuit panels.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Curtain coat liquid photo-imageable solder resist; expose bond pad openings; deposit Electroless Nickel (3µm), Electroless Palladium (0.1µm), and Immersion Gold (0.03µm) (ENEPIG finish).
processSteps.output: Corrosion-resistant ENEPIG bond pads certified for ultra-fine gold and copper wire bonding.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We coat the board with green protective lacquer, leaving exposed copper pads plated with nickel, palladium, and pure gold ready for wire welding.

processSteps.stepName: High-Speed AOI, Netlist Electrical Testing & Strip Die Punching
processSteps.input: Finished panels.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: High-speed automated optical inspection checks bond pad dimensions; flying probe netlist tester checks 100% electrical continuity; precision die punch cuts panels into standard JEDEC memory strips.
processSteps.output: Certified BT memory package substrates ready for OSAT memory die attach.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Cameras and robotic electric needles test every single wire, and precision cutters punch the boards into finished memory strips ready for chip packaging.

metadata.title: Precision Stamped & Chemically Etched Semiconductor Leadframes
metadata.subtitle: High-Speed CNC Stamping, Reel-to-Reel Chemical Micro-Etching & Selective Silver/Palladium Plating for QFP, QFN & Power Packages

productSpecification.leadframeTypes: Quad Flat No-Lead (QFN), Quad Flat Package (QFP), Small Outline IC (SOIC), TO-220 / TO-247 Power Packages
productSpecification.alloyMetallurgy: High-conductivity copper alloys (C19400, C70250) & Nickel-Iron Invar (Alloy 42 - FeNi42)
productSpecification.leadCountPitch: Lead pitch down to 0.35mm (Fine-Pitch QFP) & 0.40mm (High-Density QFN) with up to 256 leads
productSpecification.dimensionalTolerance: Lead tip position tolerance < ± 15 µm, lead flatness coplanarity < 25 µm
productSpecification.selectivePlating: Spot Silver (Ag 3-5µm) on die attach/wire bond paddle & Rough micro-etched wettable flanks
productSpecification.manufacturingThroughput: High-speed stamping up to 1,200 strokes/minute on 30-ton Bruderer presses

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: Leadframes are the metallic skeleton of the semiconductor chip: they are intricate metal strips stamped or chemically etched from high-conductivity copper alloys that hold the silicon die in their center, provide anchor points for microscopic gold or copper bonding wires, and extend metal pins outside the plastic package to solder onto circuit boards. Over 60% of all microchips on Earth—including automotive microcontrollers, power MOSFETs, analog amplifiers, and motor drivers—are packaged using leadframes. Monopolized globally by Mitsui High-tec, Chang Wah Technology, Shinko Electric, and ASM Advanced Packaging Materials ($4.5 Billion market), leadframes are in surging demand across India as Tata Electronics, CG Semi, and Kaynes build automotive chip packaging plants. Establishing India's first Precision Leadframe Manufacturing Center in Sanand or Sriperumbudur captures ₹1,400 Cr market demand with 40% EBITDA margins.

keyMetrics.sellingPricePerMT: Stamped SOIC/TSSOP Leadframe: ₹4.50 / Unit ($0.055) | Fine-Pitch QFN Strip: ₹18.00 / Strip | Power TO-247: ₹12.00 / Unit

twoProductionRoutes.name: Route A: High-Speed Progressive Carbide Die Stamping
twoProductionRoutes.summary: Feeding coiled copper alloy strip (C19400) into high-speed mechanical presses (Bruderer) equipped with multi-stage tungsten carbide progressive stamping dies, punching intricate leads at 1,000 strokes/min, followed by continuous reel-to-reel selective spot silver plating.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: Coiled high-conductivity electronic copper alloy strips (C194 / C7025) and silver plating salts.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Universal gold standard for high-volume automotive and discrete packages (SOIC, SOT-23, TO-220, QFP).

twoProductionRoutes.name: Route B: Reel-to-Reel Continuous Chemical Photo-Etching
twoProductionRoutes.summary: Laminating dry film photoresist onto copper coil, optical exposure of ultra-fine lead patterns, and spraying ferric chloride acid spray to dissolve unwanted metal without mechanical stamping stress.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: Ultra-thin copper strip (0.10-0.15mm), liquid photoresist, and ferric chloride etchant.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Essential for ultra-fine-pitch leadframes (QFN, DFN) and complex thermal heat slug designs where stamping dies would bend fine leads.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Precision Stamped & Chemically Etched Semiconductor Leadframes transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: Copper Alloy Coil Receipt, De-Coiling & Precision Tension Leveling
steps.input: High-conductivity copper alloy strip coils (C19400 / C70250, thickness 0.15 - 0.25mm).
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Strip de-coiled through 19-roll precision tension leveler under controlled hydraulic tension; eliminates coil set, crossbow, and residual mechanical stress.
steps.output: Perfect-flat, stress-relieved continuous copper strip ready for high-speed stamping.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We unroll giant coils of pure copper alloy metal and run them through flattening rollers so the strip is smoother and flatter than paper.

steps.stepName: High-Speed Progressive Carbide Die Stamping
steps.input: Flattened copper strip and Bruderer 30-ton high-speed press.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Strip advances through 24-station progressive tungsten carbide die at 1,000 strokes/min; sequential punch stations pierce pilot holes, notch lead geometries, coin tie-bars, and blank leadframe profiles.
steps.output: Continuous stamped leadframe strip with sub-15µm lead dimensions.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: A super-fast punching press punches out thousands of microscopic copper pins and center mounting plates at twenty hits per second.

steps.stepName: Continuous Degreasing & Ultrasonic Surface Cleaning
steps.input: Stamped leadframe strip.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pass through alkaline electrolytic degreasing bath and ultrasonic cleaner; removes all stamping lubricant oils, followed by hot deionized water cascade rinse and warm air drying.
steps.output: Oil-free, pristine copper leadframe strip ready for selective plating.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We wash the metal strip through ultrasonic bubble baths and hot deionized water to strip off all machine grease.

steps.stepName: Reel-to-Reel Selective Spot Silver & Palladium Electroplating
steps.input: Cleaned leadframe strip and silver cyanide/methanesulfonate plating chemistry.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Strip travels through Besi Meco reel-to-reel plating line; synchronous rubber masking belt exposes strictly the die-attach paddle and inner lead tips; high-speed jet electroplating deposits 3.5µm mirror silver.
steps.output: Leadframe strip with ultra-precise spot silver plating on bonding areas.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Rubber masking belts cover the outside pins while chemical jets spray pure silver onto the tiny center pads where the chip will be glued and wired.

steps.stepName: Chemical Micro-Roughening (Adhesion Flank Treatment)
steps.input: Selectively plated leadframe strip.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pass through proprietary micro-etching bath creating nanoscale anchor textures on outer copper leads; increases mechanical locking adhesion to epoxy molding compound by 300%.
steps.output: Roughened leadframe surface preventing moisture delamination in automotive packages.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We gently etch microscopic teeth into the copper surface so that black plastic packaging will grip the metal tight and never let moisture leak in.

steps.stepName: Telecentric Vision Inspection, Strip Shearing & Vacuum Clean Packaging
steps.input: Finished plated leadframe coils.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: High-speed optical inspection checks lead pitch, silver thickness, and coplanarity; precision rotary shear cuts coils into standard 250mm strips; interleave with desiccant paper and vacuum foil seal in cleanroom.
steps.output: Certified automotive-grade leadframe strips ready for OSAT die bonding.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Laser cameras verify every microscopic pin is straight, rotary shears chop the strip into standardized plates, and robots vacuum-seal them in protective foil.

processSteps.stepName: Copper Alloy Coil Receipt, De-Coiling & Precision Tension Leveling
processSteps.input: High-conductivity copper alloy strip coils (C19400 / C70250, thickness 0.15 - 0.25mm).
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Strip de-coiled through 19-roll precision tension leveler under controlled hydraulic tension; eliminates coil set, crossbow, and residual mechanical stress.
processSteps.output: Perfect-flat, stress-relieved continuous copper strip ready for high-speed stamping.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We unroll giant coils of pure copper alloy metal and run them through flattening rollers so the strip is smoother and flatter than paper.

processSteps.stepName: High-Speed Progressive Carbide Die Stamping
processSteps.input: Flattened copper strip and Bruderer 30-ton high-speed press.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Strip advances through 24-station progressive tungsten carbide die at 1,000 strokes/min; sequential punch stations pierce pilot holes, notch lead geometries, coin tie-bars, and blank leadframe profiles.
processSteps.output: Continuous stamped leadframe strip with sub-15µm lead dimensions.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: A super-fast punching press punches out thousands of microscopic copper pins and center mounting plates at twenty hits per second.

processSteps.stepName: Continuous Degreasing & Ultrasonic Surface Cleaning
processSteps.input: Stamped leadframe strip.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pass through alkaline electrolytic degreasing bath and ultrasonic cleaner; removes all stamping lubricant oils, followed by hot deionized water cascade rinse and warm air drying.
processSteps.output: Oil-free, pristine copper leadframe strip ready for selective plating.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We wash the metal strip through ultrasonic bubble baths and hot deionized water to strip off all machine grease.

processSteps.stepName: Reel-to-Reel Selective Spot Silver & Palladium Electroplating
processSteps.input: Cleaned leadframe strip and silver cyanide/methanesulfonate plating chemistry.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Strip travels through Besi Meco reel-to-reel plating line; synchronous rubber masking belt exposes strictly the die-attach paddle and inner lead tips; high-speed jet electroplating deposits 3.5µm mirror silver.
processSteps.output: Leadframe strip with ultra-precise spot silver plating on bonding areas.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Rubber masking belts cover the outside pins while chemical jets spray pure silver onto the tiny center pads where the chip will be glued and wired.

processSteps.stepName: Chemical Micro-Roughening (Adhesion Flank Treatment)
processSteps.input: Selectively plated leadframe strip.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pass through proprietary micro-etching bath creating nanoscale anchor textures on outer copper leads; increases mechanical locking adhesion to epoxy molding compound by 300%.
processSteps.output: Roughened leadframe surface preventing moisture delamination in automotive packages.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We gently etch microscopic teeth into the copper surface so that black plastic packaging will grip the metal tight and never let moisture leak in.

processSteps.stepName: Telecentric Vision Inspection, Strip Shearing & Vacuum Clean Packaging
processSteps.input: Finished plated leadframe coils.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: High-speed optical inspection checks lead pitch, silver thickness, and coplanarity; precision rotary shear cuts coils into standard 250mm strips; interleave with desiccant paper and vacuum foil seal in cleanroom.
processSteps.output: Certified automotive-grade leadframe strips ready for OSAT die bonding.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Laser cameras verify every microscopic pin is straight, rotary shears chop the strip into standardized plates, and robots vacuum-seal them in protective foil.

metadata.subtitle: Continuous Casting, Precision Diamond Die Wire Drawing & Annealing of Ultra-Fine 15µm - 25µm Interconnect Wire

productSpecification.wireMaterials: 4N Gold (Au ≥ 99.99%), 6N Copper (Cu ≥ 99.9999%), Palladium-Coated Copper (PCC Wire), Silver Alloy (Ag 96-99%)
productSpecification.wireDiameter: Ultra-fine 15µm to 25µm (Thinner than human hair) with diameter tolerance ± 0.3 µm
productSpecification.tensileStrengthElongation: Breaking load 8 - 18 grams, elongation 8 - 18% with uniform Free Air Ball (FAB) formation
productSpecification.palladiumCoatingThickness: PCC Wire: 20nm - 50nm uniform continuous noble palladium coating preventing copper oxidation
productSpecification.surfaceDefectStandard: Zero surface micro-scratches, die marks, or chemical residues detected via online eddy current sensors
productSpecification.spoolPackaging: Cleanroom precision wound on standardized AL-spools (1,000 to 5,000 meters per spool) vacuum foil sealed

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: Bonding wire is the electrical micro-cable that connects the silicon chip to the outside world: using supersonic vibrations and heat, high-speed wire bonding robots weld microscopic strands of ultra-pure metal wire—often only 18 to 25 microns in diameter (four times thinner than a human hair)—between the aluminum/copper bond pads on the silicon die and the leads of the package frame, completing up to 20 electrical welds every single second. While ultra-pure 4N gold wire has been the historical standard, modern semiconductor manufacturing has largely migrated to Palladium-Coated Copper (PCC) wire and Silver alloys, which offer 80% lower material cost and higher electrical/thermal conductivity. Monopolized globally by Heraeus Electronics, Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo, MK Electron, and Nippon Micrometal ($3.8 Billion market), India imports 100% of its semiconductor bonding wire. Setting up India's first Precision Bonding Wire Drawing Plant in Sanand or Bengaluru captures ₹1,250 Cr market demand with 42% EBITDA margins.

keyMetrics.marketOpportunity: ₹1,800 Cr ($220M) addressable Indian OSAT bonding wire market by 2030
keyMetrics.importDependency: 100% foreign import dependence (Germany, Japan, South Korea, Singapore)
keyMetrics.sellingPricePerMT: Gold Wire (4N): ₹75,00,000 / kg ($90,000/kg) | Palladium-Coated Copper (PCC): ₹9,50,000 / kg | Silver Alloy Wire: ₹22,00,000 / kg
keyMetrics.directCostPerMT: Blended direct production cost ₹11,50,000 per kg equivalent
keyMetrics.primaryIndianClusters: Sanand GIDC (Gujarat - adjacent to Micron & CG Semi OSAT) & Bengaluru (Karnataka)

twoProductionRoutes.summary: Melting 6N copper in vacuum induction furnace, horizontal continuous casting into 8mm rod, electrolytic continuous palladium electroplating (30nm coating), cascaded drawing through 40 natural/synthetic diamond dies down to 18µm, followed by continuous in-line induction annealing under reducing hydrogen gas.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: 6N electronic copper cathode, palladium plating salts, and electronic hydrogen gas.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Universal benchmark for 85% of modern high-volume automotive, logic, and memory wire bonding.

twoProductionRoutes.summary: Melting 99.99% pure gold with micro-dopants (Be, Ca, La < 30 ppm) to control grain boundary sliding, casting 6mm rod, multi-pass drawing through diamond dies, and protective spooling.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: 4N sovereign gold bullion from domestic refineries and micro-dopant master alloys.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Essential for high-reliability aerospace, defense (ISRO / DRDO), and military-grade hermetic packages.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Semiconductor Bonding Wires (4N Gold, Copper, Silver & PCC Wire) transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: Ultra-High Vacuum Induction Melting & Horizontal Continuous Casting
steps.input: 6N Electronic Copper Cathode (99.9999% Cu) or 4N Gold Bullion.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Induction melting at 1,150°C under 10⁻⁵ mbar vacuum; molten metal passes through graphite die under argon blanket, continuously casting an 8.0mm oxygen-free rod with grain size < 50µm.
steps.output: Continuous 8.0mm high-purity master alloy casting rod.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We melt ultra-pure copper or gold in a vacuum furnace and freeze it through a graphite mold into an endless smooth metal rod.

steps.stepName: Heavy & Intermediate Multi-Pass Wire Drawing (8.0mm down to 0.25mm)
steps.input: Cast 8.0mm rod and synthetic diamond dies.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pass through 18 consecutive tungsten carbide and diamond dies with synthetic ester lubricants; cold drawing reduces diameter to 0.25mm; intermediate annealing relieves work hardening.
steps.output: 0.25mm intermediate wire coils ready for fine drawing.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Heavy pulling machines pull the metal rod through smaller and smaller diamond funnel holes, stretching it thinner until it reaches the thickness of a needle.

steps.stepName: Continuous Reel-to-Reel Palladium Electroplating (PCC Wire)
steps.input: 0.25mm intermediate copper wire and palladium plating bath.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Wire passes continuously through electrolytic palladium bath at 10 m/s; electrodeposits an ultra-thin 30nm uniform noble palladium layer protecting copper from atmospheric oxidation.
steps.output: Palladium-coated intermediate copper wire.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We run the wire through chemical plating showers, coating it with a microscopic jacket of pure palladium so the copper won't rust.

steps.stepName: High-Speed Fine Diamond Die Micro-Drawing (down to 18µm)
steps.input: Palladium-coated wire and single-crystal natural diamond dies.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Niehoff multi-die drawing machine pulls wire through 22 cascaded natural diamond dies at 25 m/s; final die accurately sizes wire to 18.0 ± 0.2 µm with sub-nanometer surface finish.
steps.output: 18-micron ultra-fine bonding wire (four times thinner than human hair).
steps.plainEnglishDescription: A super-fast machine pulls the wire through microscopic natural diamond holes at highway speeds, thinning it down until it is four times thinner than a human hair.

steps.stepName: Continuous In-Line Hydrogen Tube Annealing & Ductility Tuning
steps.input: Hard-drawn 18µm wire.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: In-line vertical quartz tube furnace at 650°C under 100% reducing hydrogen atmosphere; controls recrystallization to tune tensile breaking load (12.5g) and elongation (12%) for high-speed bonder looping.
steps.output: Soft, ductile bonding wire certified for zero necking or wire sweep.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: The hair-thin wire shoots through a glowing hydrogen furnace pipe, softening the metal so it can bend into perfect loops without snapping.

steps.stepName: Precision Cleanroom Spooling, K&S Bondability Test & Vacuum Packaging
steps.input: Annealed wire and precision AL-spools.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Computerized level-winder spools 5,000 meters per spool; test sample run on K&S automatic wire bonder verifying Free Air Ball (FAB) sphericity and 20 welds/sec speed; spools double vacuum sealed in cleanroom.
steps.output: Certified semiconductor bonding wire spools ready for fab wire bonders.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Robots wind thousands of meters onto aluminum spools, test-weld sample balls with electric sparks, and vacuum-pack the spools for cleanroom delivery.

processSteps.output: Continuous 8.0mm high-purity master alloy casting rod.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We melt ultra-pure copper or gold in a vacuum furnace and freeze it through a graphite mold into an endless smooth metal rod.

processSteps.stepName: Heavy & Intermediate Multi-Pass Wire Drawing (8.0mm down to 0.25mm)
processSteps.input: Cast 8.0mm rod and synthetic diamond dies.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Pass through 18 consecutive tungsten carbide and diamond dies with synthetic ester lubricants; cold drawing reduces diameter to 0.25mm; intermediate annealing relieves work hardening.
processSteps.output: 0.25mm intermediate wire coils ready for fine drawing.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Heavy pulling machines pull the metal rod through smaller and smaller diamond funnel holes, stretching it thinner until it reaches the thickness of a needle.

processSteps.stepName: Continuous Reel-to-Reel Palladium Electroplating (PCC Wire)
processSteps.input: 0.25mm intermediate copper wire and palladium plating bath.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Wire passes continuously through electrolytic palladium bath at 10 m/s; electrodeposits an ultra-thin 30nm uniform noble palladium layer protecting copper from atmospheric oxidation.
processSteps.output: Palladium-coated intermediate copper wire.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: We run the wire through chemical plating showers, coating it with a microscopic jacket of pure palladium so the copper won't rust.

processSteps.stepName: High-Speed Fine Diamond Die Micro-Drawing (down to 18µm)
processSteps.input: Palladium-coated wire and single-crystal natural diamond dies.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Niehoff multi-die drawing machine pulls wire through 22 cascaded natural diamond dies at 25 m/s; final die accurately sizes wire to 18.0 ± 0.2 µm with sub-nanometer surface finish.
processSteps.output: 18-micron ultra-fine bonding wire (four times thinner than human hair).
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: A super-fast machine pulls the wire through microscopic natural diamond holes at highway speeds, thinning it down until it is four times thinner than a human hair.

processSteps.stepName: Continuous In-Line Hydrogen Tube Annealing & Ductility Tuning
processSteps.input: Hard-drawn 18µm wire.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: In-line vertical quartz tube furnace at 650°C under 100% reducing hydrogen atmosphere; controls recrystallization to tune tensile breaking load (12.5g) and elongation (12%) for high-speed bonder looping.
processSteps.output: Soft, ductile bonding wire certified for zero necking or wire sweep.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: The hair-thin wire shoots through a glowing hydrogen furnace pipe, softening the metal so it can bend into perfect loops without snapping.

processSteps.stepName: Precision Cleanroom Spooling, K&S Bondability Test & Vacuum Packaging
processSteps.input: Annealed wire and precision AL-spools.
processSteps.chemistryAndPhysics: Computerized level-winder spools 5,000 meters per spool; test sample run on K&S automatic wire bonder verifying Free Air Ball (FAB) sphericity and 20 welds/sec speed; spools double vacuum sealed in cleanroom.
processSteps.output: Certified semiconductor bonding wire spools ready for fab wire bonders.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Robots wind thousands of meters onto aluminum spools, test-weld sample balls with electric sparks, and vacuum-pack the spools for cleanroom delivery.

productSpecification.alloyCompositions: Lead-Free SAC305 (Sn96.5/Ag3.0/Cu0.5), SAC105, Low-Temp Sn-58Bi, and Gold-Tin (Au80Sn20)
productSpecification.sphereDiameterSizes: Standard BGA Spheres (0.25mm - 0.76mm) & Advanced Micro-Bumps (30µm - 80µm) for 2.5D/3D Packaging
productSpecification.diameterSphericityTolerance: Sphericity > 99.5%, diameter variation < ± 5µm for standard spheres (± 1.5µm for micro-bumps)
productSpecification.surfaceOxideContent: Oxygen content < 15 ppm (Ultra-low oxide preventing solder ball head-in-pillow HIP defects)
productSpecification.alphaParticleEmission: Ultra-Low Alpha (ULA: < 0.001 counts/cm²·hr) certified for cosmic ray soft-error immunity in DRAM
productSpecification.packagingStandard: Sealed in argon-purged ESD jars (250,000 to 1,000,000 spheres per bottle) with desiccant indicator

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: Sputtered or dropped onto the underside of microchips, solder balls are the electrical feet upon which the chip stands: when heated in an infrared reflow oven at 245°C, thousands of microscopic spherical alloy balls melt simultaneously, forming liquid solder joints that anchor the chip to the printed circuit board while conducting billions of electrical signals every second. Advanced flip-chip packaging and high-bandwidth memory (HBM3e) require hundreds of thousands of microscopic 'micro-bumps' as small as 30 microns in diameter. If a solder ball has even a tiny surface oxide skin or emits a single alpha particle from trace lead impurities, it can corrupt computer data or cause fatal open joints. Monopolized globally by Senju Metal Industry, Accurus Scientific, DS Hi-Metal, and Indium Corporation (.4 Billion market), establishing India's first Semiconductor Solder Sphere and Paste facility in Sanand GIDC supplies Micron Sanand and Tata OSATs with 44% EBITDA margins.

keyMetrics.marketOpportunity: ₹1,400 Cr (70M) addressable Indian OSAT solder consumable market by 2030
keyMetrics.importDependency: 100% foreign import dependence (Japan, Taiwan, South Korea, USA)

twoProductionRoutes.suitability: High-volume, continuous synthesis of fine solder alloy powder for paste flux blending.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Semiconductor BGA Solder Balls, Micro-Bumps & Lead-Free Pastes transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: Ultra-Pure Alloy Melting & Vacuum Chemical De-Oxidation
steps.input: Ultra-pure Tin (Sn ≥ 99.999%), Fine Silver (Ag ≥ 99.99%), and Copper master alloy.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Induction melting at 350°C under 10⁻⁴ mbar vacuum; molten SAC305 bath stirred electromagnetically to achieve exact stoichiometric homogeneity (Ag 3.0 ± 0.1%, Cu 0.5 ± 0.05%); vacuum degassing strips dissolved oxygen to < 5 ppm.
steps.output: Homogenized, de-oxidized molten SAC305 solder alloy bath.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We melt pure tin, silver, and copper inside a vacuum furnace, stirring it like liquid glass until every microscopic drop has the exact same recipe.

steps.stepName: High-Frequency Ultrasonic Piezo Droplet Jetting
steps.input: Molten SAC305 alloy.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Molten alloy forced through 150µm laser-drilled ruby/tungsten orifices vibrated by 20 kHz ultrasonic piezo transducers; Rayleigh droplet breakup generates 100,000 perfectly identical liquid spheres per second.
steps.output: Uniform liquid alloy micro-droplets in free fall.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: A vibrating ultrasonic needle pulses the liquid metal through a microscopic nozzle, pinching off a hundred thousand identical liquid metal beads every second.

steps.stepName: Thermal Inert Quenching & Spheroidization in Silicon Oil Bath
steps.input: Liquid alloy micro-droplets.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Droplets fall through counter-current column of high-purity silicon oil maintained under nitrogen blanket; surface tension snaps liquid into perfect spheres (> 99.5% sphericity) before freezing solid at 217°C.
steps.output: Solid, pristine spherical solder alloy balls.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: The droplets fall through warm oil, where surface tension pulls them into perfect shiny round balls before they freeze solid.

steps.stepName: Centrifugal Solvent De-Oiling & Cleanroom Vacuum Drying
steps.input: Solid solder balls coated with silicon oil.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: High-speed centrifuge spins off bulk oil; continuous ultrasonic wash in electronic isopropanol (IPA) dissolves residual oil films; nitrogen vacuum drying chamber removes solvent at 40°C.
steps.output: Clean, dry, oil-free solder spheres with surface oxygen < 15 ppm.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We spin the balls in a high-speed centrifuge, wash off every trace of oil with alcohol, and bake them dry under nitrogen gas.

steps.stepName: Roller Sizing Classification & Optical Sphericity Sorting
steps.input: Cleaned solder balls.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Cascaded counter-rotating precision tungsten carbide tapered rollers sort spheres into strict ± 5µm diameter bins; high-speed vision camera rejects any irregular or misshapen balls.
steps.output: Sized, defect-free solder spheres matching exact JEDEC/fab diameter specs.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: The balls roll down gap-calibrated spinning steel rollers that sort them by microscopic size bins, and cameras kick out any lumpy ones.

steps.stepName: Alpha Counting Certification & Argon-Purged Cleanroom Bottling
steps.input: Sized solder balls and cleanroom ESD bottles.
steps.chemistryAndPhysics: Batch sample tested on Ortec alpha spectrometer verifying < 0.001 counts/cm²·hr; automated cleanroom bottling under filtered argon blanket; hermetic induction foil seal with humidity indicator card.
steps.output: Certified semiconductor BGA solder balls ready for fab ball attach tools.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: We test for radiation leaks, pour the balls into static-free bottles, pump in pure argon gas, and seal the caps airtight for cleanroom shipping.

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: If silicon is the brain and substrate is the skeleton, Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) is the protective body and armor of the semiconductor chip: it is a highly specialized thermoset composite made of ortho-cresol novolac or biphenyl epoxy resins densely packed with 88% spherical fused silica beads that hermetically seals the delicate microscopic silicon die and gold/copper bonding wires from moisture, physical impact, thermal shock, and ionic corrosion. Without EMC, microchips would crumble or short-circuit in weeks. Highly consolidated globally among Sumitomo Bakelite, Resonac (Show Denko), Hysol Huawei, and Chang Chun ($3.8 Billion market), EMC is consumed in massive tonnages by every OSAT plant. With Micron Sanand, Tata Electronics OSAT (Assam), CG Semi, and Kaynes requiring over 4,500 MTPA of EMC, setting up India's first Ultra-Low-Alpha EMC compounding facility in Dahej PCPIR (Gujarat) captures ₹1,250 Cr market demand with 43% EBITDA margins.

keyMetrics.marketOpportunity: ₹1,850 Cr ($225M) Indian addressable OSAT encapsulant & underfill market by 2030
keyMetrics.importDependency: 100% foreign import dependence (Japan, Taiwan, South Korea, China)

keyMetrics.directCostPerMT: Blended direct production cost ₹7,20,000 per MT

twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: Ortho-cresol novolac epoxy, spherical fused silica (Denka), phenolic hardener, imidazole catalyst.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Universal high-volume standard for 90% of leadframe and BGA encapsulation (QFP, QFN, BGA, discrete packages).

twoProductionRoutes.name: Route B: High-Purity Liquid Capillary Underfill (CUF) Formulation
twoProductionRoutes.summary: Liquid blending of low-viscosity cycloaliphatic / bisphenol epoxies with nano-scale monodisperse silica in high-vacuum planetary deaeration mixers, formulating high-flow capillary underfills that wick beneath flip-chip dies.
twoProductionRoutes.feedstock: High-purity liquid epoxy resin, nano-silica dispersion, latent curing amine accelerators.
twoProductionRoutes.suitability: Critical for flip-chip BGA, 2.5D/3D chiplets, and wafer-level packaging where solid transfer molding cannot penetrate 30µm die clearance.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Epoxy Molding Compound (EMC) & Semiconductor Underfills transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: Raw Material Weighing & Inert Atmospheric Blending
steps.input: Solid ortho-cresol novolac epoxy, spherical silica, phenol novolac hardener, silane coupler.
steps.output: Homogeneous pre-blend dry powder with moisture < 0.05%.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Solid epoxy flakes, phenolic curing agents, silane surface-coupling chemicals, and ultra-pure spherical silica beads are gravimetrically weighed under dry nitrogen and blended in high-speed conical mixers.
steps.parameters: Nitrogen dew point < -40°C, mixing cycle 12 minutes, ambient RH < 25%.

steps.stepName: High-Shear Continuous Melt Kneading & Dispersion
steps.input: Pre-blended dry resin/silica powder mix.
steps.output: Molten, perfectly dispersed epoxy-silica composite paste.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: The dry mix enters the Buss continuous co-kneader where gentle controlled heating melts the epoxy resin at 90-110°C, coating each silica particle and dispersing pigments and flame retardants without triggering chemical cross-linking.
steps.parameters: Barrel temperature profile 85°C - 105°C, residence time 45-60 seconds, screw speed 120 RPM.

steps.stepName: Roller Calendering & Rapid Chilled Sheet Formation
steps.input: Molten compounded epoxy composite.
steps.output: Continuous solid chilled brittle composite sheets (thickness 3-5mm).
steps.plainEnglishDescription: The molten dough is squeezed between two chilled chrome-plated stainless steel rollers cooled to 10°C, instantly quenching the material into solid sheets to freeze the polymer reaction dead in its tracks.
steps.parameters: Roller chill temperature 10°C - 12°C, sheet cooling rate > 20°C/second.

steps.stepName: Cryogenic Crushing & Cleanroom Pellet Tableting
steps.input: Cooled brittle composite sheets.
steps.output: Dense, cylindrical solid EMC pellets (diameters 15mm to 45mm).
steps.plainEnglishDescription: The chilled sheets pass through hammer granulators producing uniform granules, which are fed into high-speed rotary presses that squeeze the powder into rock-hard cylindrical pellets tailored for transfer molding presses.
steps.parameters: Pellet density 1.85 - 2.05 g/cm3, pellet weight tolerance ± 0.5%, hardness > 85 Shore D.

steps.stepName: Hermetic Vacuum Aluminum Foil Packaging & Cold Storage
steps.input: Solid EMC pellets and formulated liquid underfill syringes.
steps.output: Hermetically sealed moisture-proof canisters and boxes stored at -20°C.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Pellets are vacuum-sealed inside multi-layer aluminum barrier pouches flushed with dry nitrogen to prevent atmospheric moisture absorption, then transferred into cold storage freezers at -20°C.
steps.parameters: Vacuum level < 5 mbar, nitrogen residual O2 < 0.1%, storage temperature -20°C ± 2°C.

steps.stepName: Comprehensive Quality Assurance & Lot Certification
steps.input: Random lot samples from each production batch.
steps.output: Certified QA Certificate of Analysis (CoA) for OSAT release.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: QA engineers measure spiral flow distance, gel time, mold shrinkage, hydrolyzable chloride ion content via ion chromatography, and alpha particle count before approving shipment to chip packaging lines.
steps.parameters: Spiral flow 95 ± 10 cm, gel time 32 ± 4 sec @ 175°C, Cl- < 5 ppm, alpha < 0.001 cph/cm2.

processSteps.stepName: Raw Material Weighing & Inert Atmospheric Blending
processSteps.input: Solid ortho-cresol novolac epoxy, spherical silica, phenol novolac hardener, silane coupler.
processSteps.output: Homogeneous pre-blend dry powder with moisture < 0.05%.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Solid epoxy flakes, phenolic curing agents, silane surface-coupling chemicals, and ultra-pure spherical silica beads are gravimetrically weighed under dry nitrogen and blended in high-speed conical mixers.
processSteps.parameters: Nitrogen dew point < -40°C, mixing cycle 12 minutes, ambient RH < 25%.

processSteps.stepName: High-Shear Continuous Melt Kneading & Dispersion
processSteps.input: Pre-blended dry resin/silica powder mix.
processSteps.output: Molten, perfectly dispersed epoxy-silica composite paste.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: The dry mix enters the Buss continuous co-kneader where gentle controlled heating melts the epoxy resin at 90-110°C, coating each silica particle and dispersing pigments and flame retardants without triggering chemical cross-linking.
processSteps.parameters: Barrel temperature profile 85°C - 105°C, residence time 45-60 seconds, screw speed 120 RPM.

processSteps.stepName: Roller Calendering & Rapid Chilled Sheet Formation
processSteps.input: Molten compounded epoxy composite.
processSteps.output: Continuous solid chilled brittle composite sheets (thickness 3-5mm).
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: The molten dough is squeezed between two chilled chrome-plated stainless steel rollers cooled to 10°C, instantly quenching the material into solid sheets to freeze the polymer reaction dead in its tracks.
processSteps.parameters: Roller chill temperature 10°C - 12°C, sheet cooling rate > 20°C/second.

processSteps.stepName: Cryogenic Crushing & Cleanroom Pellet Tableting
processSteps.input: Cooled brittle composite sheets.
processSteps.output: Dense, cylindrical solid EMC pellets (diameters 15mm to 45mm).
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: The chilled sheets pass through hammer granulators producing uniform granules, which are fed into high-speed rotary presses that squeeze the powder into rock-hard cylindrical pellets tailored for transfer molding presses.
processSteps.parameters: Pellet density 1.85 - 2.05 g/cm3, pellet weight tolerance ± 0.5%, hardness > 85 Shore D.

processSteps.stepName: Hermetic Vacuum Aluminum Foil Packaging & Cold Storage
processSteps.input: Solid EMC pellets and formulated liquid underfill syringes.
processSteps.output: Hermetically sealed moisture-proof canisters and boxes stored at -20°C.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: Pellets are vacuum-sealed inside multi-layer aluminum barrier pouches flushed with dry nitrogen to prevent atmospheric moisture absorption, then transferred into cold storage freezers at -20°C.
processSteps.parameters: Vacuum level < 5 mbar, nitrogen residual O2 < 0.1%, storage temperature -20°C ± 2°C.

processSteps.stepName: Comprehensive Quality Assurance & Lot Certification
processSteps.input: Random lot samples from each production batch.
processSteps.output: Certified QA Certificate of Analysis (CoA) for OSAT release.
processSteps.plainEnglishDescription: QA engineers measure spiral flow distance, gel time, mold shrinkage, hydrolyzable chloride ion content via ion chromatography, and alpha particle count before approving shipment to chip packaging lines.
processSteps.parameters: Spiral flow 95 ± 10 cm, gel time 32 ± 4 sec @ 175°C, Cl- < 5 ppm, alpha < 0.001 cph/cm2.

executiveSummary.plainEnglishOverview: As AI GPUs, data center CPUs, and electric vehicle power modules push power densities beyond 500 Watts per chip, heat becomes the ultimate killer of computing performance. Thermal Interface Materials (TIM) and metallic Heat Spreaders (Lids) are the critical thermal escape highways of the semiconductor: stamped from oxygen-free high-conductivity copper and plated with anti-corrosion nickel, the rigid lid protects the fragile silicon die while an ultra-pure indium solder preform (TIM1) conducts heat directly off the die at blazing speed (> 80 W/m·K). Without ultra-flat heat spreaders and high-conductivity TIMs, modern AI supercomputers and EV inverters would melt their solder joints in seconds. Monopolized globally by Cooler Master, Foxconn, Indium Corporation, Honeywell Electronic Materials, and Shin-Etsu ($3.2 Billion market), demand is surging in India as Tata Electronics, CG Semi, and automotive Tier-1s expand. Building India's first Precision Heat Spreader & Advanced TIM Manufacturing Hub in Sanand/Hosur captures ₹1,100 Cr market demand with 41% EBITDA margins.

manufacturingProcess.plainEnglishSummary: Manufacturing Semiconductor Thermal Interface Materials (TIM1/TIM2) & Heat Spreaders (Lids) transforms basic raw materials into ultra-pure semiconductor inputs through precision multi-stage physical and chemical operations.

steps.stepName: OFHC Copper Strip Slitting & Precision Progressive Stamping
steps.input: Coiled oxygen-free copper strip (C10200, thickness 1.5 - 2.5 mm).
steps.output: Formed copper heat spreader blanks with cavity pockets and lip steps.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: High-purity oxygen-free copper coil is automatically uncoiled, leveled, and fed into the 200-ton Bruderer press where multi-stage carbide dies stamp out the external dimensions, inner die cavity recess, and perimeter sealant grooves.
steps.parameters: Stamping stroke rate 250 strokes/min, dimensional tolerance ± 15 µm, tool die life 2,000,000 strokes.

steps.stepName: Controlled Atmosphere Stress-Relief Annealing
steps.input: Stamped copper heat spreader blanks.
steps.output: Stress-relieved, ductile copper blanks with stabilized grain structure.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: The stamped lids pass through a continuous mesh-belt furnace heated to 450°C under a protective nitrogen-hydrogen blanket to relieve cold-working stress, ensuring the metal will never distort or warp during soldering.
steps.parameters: Furnace temperature 450°C ± 5°C, atmosphere 95% N2 / 5% H2, cycle time 45 minutes.

steps.stepName: Double-Sided Precision Lapping & Deburring
steps.input: Annealed copper heat spreader lids.
steps.output: Ultra-flat lids with surface flatness < 10 µm and mirror finish.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Lids are placed into planetary workholder wheels between rotating upper and lower cast-iron lapping plates charged with diamond micro-abrasives, grinding both faces perfectly parallel to remove any stamping burrs.
steps.parameters: Lapping slurry 3µm polycrystalline diamond, plate speed 45 RPM, surface roughness Ra < 0.2 µm.

steps.stepName: Multi-Stage Ultrasonic Cleaning & Electrolytic Nickel Plating
steps.input: Lapped and deburred copper lids.
steps.output: Corrosion-resistant nickel-plated heat spreaders (3-5µm Ni + optional flash gold).
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Lids are racked and dipped through ultrasonic degreasing, acid etching, and an electrolytic nickel sulfamate plating bath to deposit a microscopic 4-micron nickel barrier that prevents copper oxidation and solder corrosion.
steps.parameters: Nickel plating thickness 3.5 - 5.0 µm, current density 3-5 A/dm2, adhesion test per ASTM B571 (no peeling).

steps.stepName: High-Purity Indium Foil Rolling & Die-Cutting (TIM1)
steps.input: Electronic grade 5N Indium ingots.
steps.output: Precision die-cut Indium preforms (thickness 50µm ± 3µm).
steps.plainEnglishDescription: In parallel, 99.999% pure indium metal is cold-rolled through ultra-precision polished rollers into thin ribbons, then stamped with micro-dies into exact rectangular preforms matching the silicon chip dimensions.
steps.parameters: Foil thickness 50 µm ± 3 µm, burr height < 5 µm, packaged between silicone release liners.

steps.stepName: Automated 3D Optical Flatness QA & Waffle-Pack Packaging
steps.input: Finished nickel-plated lids and cut Indium TIM preforms.
steps.output: 100% inspected, certified thermal components vacuum sealed in JEDEC matrix trays.
steps.plainEnglishDescription: Every heat spreader passes under a high-speed Zygo white-light interferometer measuring 3D warpage across 1,000 points; approved units are robotically placed into anti-static JEDEC trays and vacuum sealed.
steps.parameters: Warpage threshold < 15 µm, zero visual scratches, vacuum sealed in Class 1,000 cleanroom.
